data.name: TVS Motor Company Ltd
data.about: TVS Motor Company Ltd (TVSM) is engaged in manufacturing two-wheelers and its accessories; it currently manufactures a wide range of two-wheelers and three-wheelers.[1]

target.raw_metric: capex for new products and capacity expansion
target.quote: I think last time I highlighted, we are going for 8.3 million from the current capacity of about 6.8 million. And in 3-wheeler, we are going from 0.25 million capacity to about 0.42 million. So this is a big, big increase, and that's why we are also investing somewhere around, including our new products, we are investing about INR 3,500 crores, new products plus all the capacity expansion, which is going to come over the last, next one quarter is over second quarter, third quarter. By fourth quarter, we will reach is 8.3 million capacity.

rows.explanation: Guided capex for new products and capacity expansion ≈ ₹3,500 Cr for FY27; not checkable from reported financials.

data.what_it_does: TVS Motor Company manufactures and sells motorcycles, scooters, mopeds, and three-wheelers (both ICE and EV) in India and internationally, serving a broad spectrum of users from daily commuters to performance enthusiasts and commercial operators. Its product portfolio spans domestic and international markets with offerings across mopeds, motorcycles, petrol and electric scooters, three-wheelers, and premium motorcycles.

bull.text: Revenue and PAT have compounded at 20.6% and 34.5% CAGR over three years, reaching ₹65,579 Cr and ₹3,988 Cr TTM respectively.
Operating margin expanded from 12.6% to 14.9% over three years with ROCE at 17%, while quarterly revenue accelerated from ₹14,756 Cr in Dec 2025 to ₹19,474 Cr in Sep 2026.
Management is investing ~₹3,500 Cr to raise two-wheeler capacity from 6.8M to 8.3M and three-wheeler capacity from 0.25M to 0.42M by Q4, targeting scooter growth above 40%.

bear.text: Leverage is high with debt-to-equity at 3.48, and operating cash flow has covered only 56% of PAT over three years, flagging poor cash conversion.
Capex of ~₹3,500 Cr for next year will keep cash flows pressured, though management expects it to decline by ₹500-600 Cr thereafter.
Management admits only 35% of cost increases were offset by price hikes, leaving a 3-5% margin headwind.
